analysis: The PR modifies only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. Per file_changes, the single change adds three rows (head lines ~1756-1758) to the environment-variable forwarding table: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. Each maps to a source constant (GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift idleCacheSweepEnvironmentKey; EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift segmentRetentionEnvironmentKey and segmentHostZerosEnvironmentKey). The supplied base units (lines 1-824) do not include that region, so I could not see the surrounding table header or the semantics of the three variables. The change is documentation-only, with no executable code, auth, encryption, or attestation changes visible. The new variables concern TTFT, KV segment retention and host-side zeroing. They could touch T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and T-041 (prefix-cache, TTFT oracle) if the underlying Swift changes alter KV retention or zeroing defaults. Those source changes are not in this batch, so I cannot confirm whether SEGMENT_RETENTION or SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS weakens residual-data hygiene, or whether forwarding them into launchd lets a local operator change behavior (the operator is already within the ADV-001 trust assumptions). The base text in the supplied units (e.g. the cache section, lines 63-85) is unchanged and its claims about the SSD cache remain consistent with T-041. No regression is identified from the docs change itself. Integration should check the corresponding Swift changes, in particular whether segment retention or skipped host zeroing affects T-028 or the T-041 cache-scoping and TTL postures.
